zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ — some people said: "اَلتَّسْبِيحُ" (glorification) is the traces of (divine) workmanship in the heavens and in the earth and in those within them; and in the same way they interpreted His saying: ﴿وَإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 44]. This is an error. "اَلتَّسْبِيحُ" is glorifying Allah and declaring Him free of evil. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 44]: if tasbīḥ were the traces of workmanship, it would be intelligible and they would understand it. Further evidence for this view is His saying: ﴿وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الجِبالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ والطَّيْرَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 79]: if their tasbīḥ were the traces of workmanship, there would be no point in His saying ﴿وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الجِبالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ والطَّيْرَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 79].

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما لَكم ألا تُنْفِقُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ولِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ — its interpretation is: what do you gain by abandoning spending on what brings near to Allah, when you are going to die and leave your wealth behind?
His saying: ﴿لا يَسْتَوِي مِنكم مَن أنْفَقَ مِن قَبْلِ الفَتْحِ وقاتَلَ أُولَئِكَ أعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أنْفَقُوا مِن بَعْدُ وقاتَلُوا﴾ — because whoever was earlier in believing in Allah and His Messenger, upon him be peace, and affirmed him, is better than whoever came with belief and affirmation after him; for the earlier ones suffered more hardship than those after them, and so their insight was also more penetrating. And He said: ﴿وَكُلا وعَدَ اللَّهُ الحُسْنى﴾, except that He made known the superiority of the one who preceded to belief over the one who came later.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضاعِفُهُ لَهُ" — it is also read ﴿فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ﴾ with the accusative (naṣb). Whoever reads the accusative does so as the answer to the interrogative with the fāʾ; whoever reads the nominative does so by conjunction (ʿaṭf) onto "يُقْرِضُ", or it may be resumptive (istiʾnāf), on the meaning: "فَهُوَ يُضاعِفُهُ لَهُ" (then He multiplies it for him). The meaning of ﴿يُقْرِضُ﴾ here is: he does a good deed in following the command of Allah and obeying Him. The Arabs say to anyone who has done them good: "قَدْ أحْسَنْتَ قَرْضِي" (you have made me a fine loan) and "قَدْ أقْرَضْتَنِي قَرْضًا حَسَنًا" (you have lent me a goodly loan), when he has done him good. The poet said:
وَإذا جُوزِيتَ قَرْضًا فاجْزِهِ ∗∗∗ إنَّما يَجْزِي الفَتى غَيْرَ الجَمَلْ
(When you are repaid a loan (a good turn), repay it; it is only the true man, not the camel, who repays)
The meaning is: "when a kindness is done to you, requite it."

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرى المُؤْمِنِينَ والمُؤْمِناتِ يَسْعى نُورُهم بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وبِأيْمانِهِمْ﴾ — "يَوْمَ" is accusative (manṣūb) by His saying: ﴿فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ ولَهُ أجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 11], on that day.
The meaning of ﴿يَسْعى نُورُهم بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وبِأيْمانِهِمْ﴾ is: in the sense of "their light is before them", and it is the sign of their righteous hands (deeds). ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 8], that is: make it bring us to Your Paradise.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُولُ المُنافِقُونَ والمُنافِقاتُ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا انْظُرُونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِن نُورِكُمْ﴾ — it has been read "أنْظِرُونا", with the disjunctive alif (qaṭʿ) and with the connective alif (waṣl). Whoever says ﴿انْظُرُونا﴾ takes it from "نَظَرَ، يَنْظُرُ", meaning: wait for us. Whoever says "أنْظِرُونا", with kasra, means: grant us respite. It has also been said that the meaning of "أنْظِرُونا" is likewise "wait for us", and the one who holds this cited the verse of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:
أبا هِنْدٍ فَلا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْنا ∗∗∗ وأنْظِرْنا نُخَبِّرْكَ اليَقِينا
(O Abū Hind, do not be hasty with us; wait for us and we will tell you the certain truth)
His saying: ﴿قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وراءَكم فالتَمِسُوا نُورًا﴾ — its interpretation is: there is no light for you with us.
His saying: ﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهم بِسُورٍ لَهُ بابٌ باطِنُهُ فِيهِ الرَّحْمَةُ وظاهِرُهُ مِن قِبَلِهِ العَذابُ﴾ — that is: the side facing the believers has mercy in it, and the side facing the disbelievers, its outside, punishment comes to them from its direction.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَكِنَّكم فَتَنْتُمْ أنْفُسَكم وتَرَبَّصْتُمْ وارْتَبْتُمْ﴾ — the meaning of ﴿فَتَنْتُمْ أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ is: you employed them in sedition (fitna); and you awaited turns of misfortune for the Prophet ﷺ and the believers. ﴿وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الأمانِيُّ﴾, that is: what you used to wish for, of misfortunes befalling the believers. ﴿حَتّى جاءَ أمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: until Allah sent down His help upon His Prophet and the believers. ﴿وَغَرَّكم بِاللَّهِ الغَرُورُ﴾, that is: Satan deceived you, and he is al-gharūr (the Deceiver), on the pattern "اَلْفَعُولُ"; "فَعُولٌ" is one of the intensive forms (asmāʾ al-mubālagha). You say "فُلانٌ أكُولٌ" when he eats much, and "ضَرُوبٌ" when he strikes much. That is why Satan is called "اَلْغَرُورُ": because he deceives the son of Adam much. If he deceives once, he is "غارٌّ"; "غارٌّ" is also suitable for much, but "غَرُورٌ" is not suitable for little. It has also been read "اَلْغُرُورُ", which is everything that deceives of the goods of this world. The meaning of "ارْتَبْتُمْ" is: you let doubt prevail over certainty.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَأْواكُمُ النّارُ هي مَوْلاكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 15] — it is more fitting for you (awlā bikum), because of the sins you committed beforehand. Similar to that is the poet's saying:
فَغَدَتْ كِلا الفَرْجَيْنِ تَحْسِبُ أنَّهُ ∗∗∗ مَوْلى المَخافَةِ خَلْفَها وأمامَها
(So she set off in the morning, reckoning that each of the two openings, behind her and before her, was the more fitting place (mawlā) of danger)
Like that, i.e.: "the mawlā of danger, behind her and before her."

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهم لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وما نَـزَلَ مِنَ الحَقِّ﴾ — it is also read ﴿وَما نَـزَلَ مِنَ الحَقِّ﴾, with the lightened form. [Translator's note: the Quranic text as printed here already shows the lightened form نَزَلَ in both places; the contrast intended is presumably with the doubled form نَزَّلَ.]
His saying ﴿يَأْنِ﴾ is from "أنى، يَأْنِي"; one also says "آنَ يَئِينُ" in this sense, and its meaning is "حانَ، يَحِينُ" (the time has come). This verse, and Allah knows best, was revealed concerning a group of the believers who were urged to tenderness, mercy and humility; as for those whom He, Mighty and Majestic is He, described with submissiveness, tenderness and mercy, they are a group of the believers above these.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا يَكُونُوا كالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ — it has also been read with tāʾ: "تَكُونُوا". ﴿فَطالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الأمَدُ فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾, that is: do not be like those whose hearts hardened when the period grew long for them.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ﴾ — that is: He gives life to the dead on the Day of Resurrection and causes the living to die in this world. "يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ" may also mean: He gives life to the sperm-drops, which are only lifeless matter, and causes the living to die. The position of ﴿يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ﴾ is nominative (rafʿ), on the meaning: "هُوَ يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ" (He gives life and causes death); and it may be accusative (naṣb), on the meaning: "His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, giving life and causing death, all-powerful" — [Translator's note: i.e. as a ḥāl (circumstantial)].

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿هُوَ الأوَّلُ والآخِرُ والظّاهِرُ والباطِنُ﴾ — its interpretation is: He is the First before everything, the Last after everything, the Manifest (al-Ẓāhir), the Knower of what is manifest, and the Hidden (al-Bāṭin), the Knower of what is hidden; as you say: "فُلانٌ يُبْطِنُ أمْرَ فُلانٍ", that is, he knows the inner workings of his affair. ﴿وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾: nothing is hidden from Him.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ في الأرْضِ﴾ — its interpretation is: He knows what enters the earth of rain and other things; ﴿وَما يَخْرُجُ مِنها﴾: of plants and other things; ﴿وَما يَنْـزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾: of provision, rain and angels; ﴿وَما يَعْرُجُ فِيها﴾, that is: what ascends to it of the deeds of the servants, and the angels who ascend.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ في النَّهارِ ويُولِجُ النَّهارَ في اللَّيْلِ﴾ — its meaning is: "He makes the night enter into the day, by decreasing the night and increasing the day"; and likewise ﴿وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ في اللَّيْلِ﴾: He decreases the day and increases the night. It is like His saying: ﴿يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلى النَّهارِ ويُكَوِّرُ النَّهارَ عَلى اللَّيْلِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 5].

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾ — its meaning is: "affirm that Allah is One and that Muhammad is His Messenger". ﴿وَأنْفِقُوا مِمّا جَعَلَكم مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ﴾, that is: spend from what He has given you possession of, and spend in the way of Allah and on what brings near to Him.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِي الأرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها قَدْ بَيَّنّا لَكُمُ الآياتِ﴾ — its meaning is that reviving the earth after its death is evidence of the oneness of Allah, and is among His signs that point to that.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ المُصَّدِّقِينَ والمُصَّدِّقاتِ﴾ — with doubling of the ṣād; its meaning is: "إنَّ المُتَصَدِّقِينَ والمُتَصَدِّقاتِ" (the men and women who give charity). It is also read "إنَّ المُصَدِّقِينَ والمُصَدِّقاتِ", with the lightened form, and its meaning is: "the believing men and believing women, of those who affirmed the truth of Allah and His Messenger and so believed in what the Prophet ﷺ brought."
His saying: ﴿وَأقْرَضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾, that is: they gave charity from good wealth. ﴿يُضاعَفُ لَهم ولَهم أجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾, that is: what they did is multiplied for them, and that multiplication is a generous reward.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورُسُلِهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصِّدِّيقُونَ﴾ — on the pattern "اَلْفِعِّيلُونَ"; its singular is "صِدِّيقٌ", which is an intensive noun (ism li-l-mubālagha) denoting the action. You say "رَجُلٌ صِدِّيقٌ": one who affirms the truth much; likewise "رَجُلٌ سِكِّيتٌ": one who is silent much. So the meaning is that the believer who affirms Allah and His messengers is the one who goes to the utmost in truthfulness.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والشُّهَداءُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ لَهم أجْرُهم ونُورُهُمْ﴾ — it may be a new (mustaʾnaf) sentence, nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject; ibtidāʾ), so the meaning is: "and the witnesses with their Lord — they have their reward and their light"; and "اَلشُّهَداءُ" are the prophets. It is also possible that "والشُّهَداءُ" be coordinated (nasaq) with what precedes it, so that the meaning is: "those are the truthful ones, and those are the witnesses with their Lord", and ﴿لَهم أجْرُهم ونُورُهُمْ﴾ then belongs to the whole group of the truthful ones and the witnesses.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اعْلَمُوا أنَّما الحَياةُ الدُّنْيا لَعِبٌ ولَهْوٌ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أعْجَبَ الكُفّارَ نَباتُهُ﴾ — the kāf is in the position of the nominative (fī mawḍiʿ rafʿ) on two counts. One of them is that it be a ṣifa (adjective), so that the meaning is: "the life of this world is only play, diversion, adornment and boasting among you, like ghayth" — which is rain. Or its nominative is as a khabar after a khabar (a second predicate), on the meaning that the life of this world and its adornment are like rain whose vegetation pleases the kuffār. "اَلْكُفّارُ" here has two interpretations. One of them is that it means the crop (al-zarʿ) [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense, as the following words show, is "the sowers" (al-zurrāʿ)]: if its vegetation pleases the sowers, despite their knowledge of it, it is at the utmost of what is admired. Or "اَلْكُفّارُ" here may be those who disbelieve in Allah, who are more intensely pleased by the adornment of this world than the believers.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَراهُ مُصْفَرًّا﴾ — the meaning of ﴿يَهِيجُ﴾ is: it begins to dry, so yellowness appears in it. ﴿ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطامًا﴾, that is: broken up, shattered and gone. Allah struck this as a parable for the passing away of this world.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَفِي الآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ ومَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ ورِضْوانٌ﴾ — it is also read "وَرُضْوانٌ"; both have been transmitted from ʿĀṣim, with ḍamma and with kasra. Its meaning is: forgiveness for the friends of Allah and punishment for His enemies.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿سابِقُوا إلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِن رَبِّكم وجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُها كَعَرْضِ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ﴾ — the meaning is: "race one another with righteous deeds". It has been said that the gardens are seven, and it has been said four, because of His saying: ﴿وَلِمَن خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 46], and His saying after that: ﴿وَمِن دُونِهِما جَنَّتانِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 62]. It has been said: (He mentioned) its breadth and did not mention its length — and Allah knows best; the mention of its breadth here is only a likening for the servants by what they do and what occurs to their minds, and the greatest thing that occurs to their minds is the extent of the heavens and the earth.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشاءُ﴾ — this is evidence that no one enters Paradise except by the bounty of Allah.

zajjaj:22-22.t: Then He informed them that what leads to Paradise or the Fire comes about only by decree and predestination (qaḍāʾ wa-qadar), and so He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما أصابَ مِن مُصِيبَةٍ في الأرْضِ ولا في أنْفُسِكم إلا في كِتابٍ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ نَبْرَأها﴾, that is: before We create it. So whatever occurs in the earth of drought or shortage, and likewise whatever occurs in souls of sickness and death, or loss in trade, or earning of good or evil, is written with Allah and known.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا عَلى ما فاتَكم ولا تَفْرَحُوا بِما آتاكُمْ﴾ — whoever reads "أتاكُمْ" means: "what has come to you"; and whoever reads ﴿آتاكُمْ﴾ means: "what He has given you". The meaning of "تَفْرَحُوا" here is: do not rejoice with an intense joy in which you become insolent and arrogant. The evidence for that is: ﴿واللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ﴾; by this He indicated that He censures the joy in which its owner swaggers and becomes arrogant. As for joy in the blessing of Allah and thanks for it, that is not blameworthy. Likewise ﴿لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ﴾, that is: do not grieve with a grief that makes you transgress, until it drives you to bind yourselves to ruin; and do not reckon, against the reward of Allah, what you are stripped of and what has escaped you. [Translator's note: the last clause is terse in the Arabic (ولا تَعْتَدُوا بِثَوابِ اللَّهِ ما تَسْلُبُونَهُ، وما فاتَكم); the rendering is tentative.]

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ ويَأْمُرُونَ النّاسَ بِالبُخْلِ﴾ — it is also read "بِالبَخْلِ", like "اَلرُّشْدُ" and "اَلرَّشَدُ". This is of two kinds. One of them, in the exegesis, is that they are those who withhold making known the description of the Prophet ﷺ which they had come to know in the Torah and the Gospel. The second option is that when He urged the ṣifa [Translator's note: so in the text (الصِّفَة, "description"); the context of spending suggests al-ṣadaqa, "charity"], He made known that as for those who withhold it and enjoin withholding it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is free of need of them.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا الحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ ومَنافِعُ لِلنّاسِ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that Adam, upon him be peace, descended to earth with the ʿalāt, the hammer and the tongs; "اَلْعُلاةُ" is what smiths call "اَلسِّنْدانَ" (the anvil).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ﴾, that is: with it one defends and with it one fights; ﴿وَمَنافِعُ لِلنّاسِ﴾: they use it in their tools, and in what they benefit from of their vessels, and in everything that is put to use.
His saying: ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَن يَنْصُرُهُ ورُسُلَهُ بِالغَيْبِ﴾, that is: so that Allah may know who fights alongside His messengers in His paths. Its interpretation and meaning have already been given.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِرُسُلِنا﴾, that is: We made messengers follow Nūḥ and Ibrāhīm after them. ﴿وَقَفَّيْنا بِعِيسى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ وآتَيْناهُ الإنْجِيلَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that Allah gave ʿĪsā the Gospel all at once.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا في قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً ورَحْمَةً﴾ — "رَآفَةً" is also permissible, on the pattern of "اَلسَّماحَةُ". Abū Zayd related that one says: "رَؤُفْتُ بِالرَّجُلِ، رَأْفَةً" (I was compassionate to the man), and that is the (accepted) reading; it has also been read "وَرَآفَةً".
His saying: ﴿وَرَهْبانِيَّةً ابْتَدَعُوها ما كَتَبْناها عَلَيْهِمْ إلا ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ﴾ — this verse is difficult in its interpretation, and its meaning, and Allah knows best, admits two kinds. One of them is that the meaning of His saying ﴿وَرَهْبانِيَّةً ابْتَدَعُوها﴾ is: they invented a monasticism, as you say: "رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا، وعَمْرًا أكْرَمْتُهُ" (I saw Zayd, and ʿAmr I honoured) [Translator's note: i.e. رَهْبانِيَّةً is accusative by a verb implied from the following one]; and ﴿ما كَتَبْناها عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ means: We did not prescribe it for them at all; and ﴿إلا ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ and alif, so the meaning is: "We prescribed for them nothing but the seeking of Allah's good pleasure", and seeking Allah's good pleasure is following what He commanded. This, and Allah knows best, is one option. There is another option in ﴿ابْتَدَعُوها﴾: it has come in the exegesis that they used to see from their kings what they could not bear, so they took to underground hideouts and hermitages; thus they invented that. And when they had bound themselves to that voluntary devotion and entered into it, its completion became binding upon them, just as when a person imposes upon himself a fast that was not made obligatory for him, he is bound to complete it.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَما رَعَوْها حَقَّ رِعايَتِها﴾ — this is of two kinds, and Allah knows best. One of them is that they fell short in what they had bound themselves to. The other — and it is better — is that when the Prophet ﷺ was sent and they did not believe in him, they were abandoning obedience to Allah, and so they did not observe that monasticism as it ought to be observed. The evidence for that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَآتَيْنا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنهم أجْرَهُمْ﴾, that is: those of them who believed in the Prophet, upon him be peace.
﴿وَكَثِيرٌ مِنهم فاسِقُونَ﴾, that is: disbelievers.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ﴾ — by "آمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ" He means: affirm the truth of His Messenger.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُؤْتِكم كِفْلَيْنِ مِن رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ — its meaning is: He will give you two shares of His mercy. Its derivation in the language is from "اَلْكِفْلُ", a cloth which the rider places beneath him when he rides pillion, so that he does not fall. So its interpretation is: He will give you two shares that protect you from the ruin of sins. ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكم نُورًا تَمْشُونَ بِهِ﴾, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نُورُهم يَسْعى بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 8]; this is the mark of the believers on the Day of Resurrection, and the evidence for that is His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُولُ المُنافِقُونَ والمُنافِقاتُ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا انْظُرُونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِن نُورِكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 13]. It is also possible, and Allah knows best, that ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكم نُورًا تَمْشُونَ بِهِ﴾ means: He will make for you a clear path of guidance by which you are guided.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ ألا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى شَيْءٍ مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — the meaning is: "Allah did that with you as He did with those of the People of the Book who believed, so that they may know"; and "لا" is for emphasis (muʾakkida). In ﴿ألا يَقْدِرُونَ﴾, the "لا" here indicates the implied (pronoun) in "أنْ", with "أنْ" being the lightened form (takhfīf); the meaning is: that they are not able (annahum lā yaqdirūn), that is: so that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah.
